blind.why: Arc idle (idle_arc.png) vs CS2 M4 (t2_031). Framing now comparable (our muzzle 0.624,0.555), but CS2's gun points into the scene with a natural diagonal forearm; ours is a side-on khaki plank held by a vertical dark forearm stump with a cream cuff ring and grey block fingers.
Arc firing (fire_arc_0.png) vs CS2 M4 firing (t4_028). Our flash star is punchy and now clear of the crosshair, but the weapon/hand read as toy blocks; CS2 frame is more cohesive.
Lance idle (idle_lance.png) vs CS2 AWP (t4_021). Ours: same khaki body as every long arm, spring-coil muzzle, mitten hand; CS2 AWP silhouette and glove read instantly.
Judge idle (dr_judge_4.png) vs CS2 pistol (t1_023). CS2 pistol sits small and low-right; our gold Judge is huge and central (muzzle 0.536,0.569), filling the lower-middle of the screen.

biggest_gap: Sidearms were left out of the r3 framing fix: they are oversized and central, so their flash blinds the crosshair on every shot. Repro: ?test=1&seed=3&match=1&phase=live, combat.give(localActor,'judge'), press slot2, fire (shots/critic-viewmodel-r3/k_judge_fire.png, fj_0.png). Judge muzzle projects to (0.536,0.569), only 3.6% right of centre; mean luminance of the 60px crosshair box goes 59 -> 233 (pure white) on the shot frame. Pip (0.592,0.621) and Twin (0.592,0.609) flash stars also cover the crosshair (57 -> 104 / 94). CS2 pistols sit small and low-right (muzzle about 0.62-0.70, 0.60-0.70) and the flash never reaches the aim point. Run fitRest for pistols too, shrink the Judge about 30%, and cap the flash radius so the glow stops short of the crosshair.
other_gaps: Hands/forearms: on every long arm the left forearm is a fat dark cylinder rising vertically from the screen bottom at x~0.72, with a cream cuff ring and grey cube fingers (idle_rail.png crop). It reads as a puppet stump. CS2's support arm enters diagonally from the lower centre, with a sleeve and glove wrapping the handguard.

Per-tagger identity in match: zip, hum, scatter, storm and lance share one khaki/gunmetal body and near-identical side-on silhouettes (idle_zip/hum/scatter/storm.png). The MP9-class Zip is as long as a rifle and Scatter reads as a rifle. Only Arc (orange trim), Halo (white) and Judge (gold) stand out.

Held utility is oversized and misread: the Haze can fills x .68-.85 / y .45-1.0 (u_idle_0.png), and Strobe is a beige can with a handle that looks like a beer mug (u_idle_1.png). CS2 grenades sit small, low-right.
Tap: at idle the bat tip sits at (0.553,0.509), right beside the crosshair (idle_tap.png). The swing trail is a thin gold spear across about 70% of the screen (melee_2/3.png).

Lance: about 50 ms after a scoped shot the unscope passes through the eyepiece pose, and the octagonal lens fills the screen centre at the moment you need to see the hit (fire_judge_1.png in the B run).
Beacon plant: the keypad face is never shown to camera, so the device reads as a grey blob with an antenna (plant_0-3.png). Walk bob/strafe sway is barely visible across walk_0-5.png.
bugs: Judge muzzle flash fully whites out the crosshair on every shot (crosshair-box luminance 59 -> 233). Pip and Twin flashes partially cover it.
Tap idle pose puts the weapon tip about 5% of screen width from the crosshair, blocking the aim point.
strengths: Long-arm framing fixed: Arc muzzle at (0.624,0.555), and over a 14-shot spray it stays in x .623-.634 / y .508-.543 with the flash clear of the crosshair
Viewmodel costs 6-7 draw calls and about 5.6-6.8k tris (107 calls with it hidden vs 113-115 shown)
Reload keeps the rifle low-right with a readable glowing-cell swap; inspect shows the whole gun mid-frame
Scope-in raise to eyepiece to clean overlay; AWP bolt cycle and auto-rescope
Punchy flash, tracer, ejected cells and smoke puffs; throw preview arc and release read well
No console errors in any live-match run
